facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old woman presented with a lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma
there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
the overlying skin was uninvolved
there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm with relatively hypoechoic, heterogeneous internal echoes
A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast cancer and has now presented with a new lump in the same breast, which has increased in size on follow-up, suggesting a possible recurrence.
The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the breast, which increases the risk of developing radiation-induced breast cancer, and the current lesion is located in the same breast.
The lesion is described as a firm, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography, which is consistent with a fibroadenoma.
The lesion is described as a lobulated, well-defined mass with hypoechoic internal echoes on ultrasonography, which could be consistent with a breast cyst.
The lesion is described as a firm, fixed mass with a focal asymmetrical density on mammography, which could be consistent with a phyllodes tumor.
The lesion is described as a well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography, which could be consistent with pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia.
The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the breast, which increases the risk of developing fat necrosis, and the current lesion is located in the same breast.
The lesion is described as a firm, fixed mass with a rapid increase in size, which could be consistent with a sarcoma.

rationales.F01: A lump in the breast is a common presentation of breast cancer recurrence.
rationales.F02: Previous radiation therapy increases the risk of radiation-induced breast cancer.
rationales.F03: A firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle is concerning for malignancy.
rationales.F08: A core-needle biopsy showing atrophic mammary glands makes breast cancer less likely.
rationales.F09: An increasing lesion size on follow-up is concerning for malignancy.
